chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal and Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from one of our companions,
that he did not rest, so Al-Rida (peace be upon him) ordered him to leave so that he might rest.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Rida order his companion to do regarding resting?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) instructs a companion to perform *muarras* (overnight stay/resting) after noticing he had not done so, emphasizing the spiritual and physical necessity of pausing during religious duties. This highlights the Shia scholarly principle that maintaining one's well-being is integral to sustained devotion, reflecting the Imam's attentive care for his followers' holistic state.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, and Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from one of our companions

that he did not rest, 
So Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> ordered him (his<sup>asws</sup> companion) that he should leave, and he should rest’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal and al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ali ibn Asbat, from certain individuals of our people
that he did not disembark for rest where the Holy Prophet had rested. Al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, commanded him to go back and do what he was supposed to do.”
